chapter: Records, dances and Blanche Calloway (repeated passages)
title: Gus Wilson and the Speed Webb band personnel
summary: They wonder what became of arranger-trombonist Gus Wilson and name Reunald Jones and Speed Dunn among the band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Gus Wilson, who was one of the arrangers, too, I guess, in that band...
Yes.
He died quite young, didn't he?
I didn't know he died! I don't think he did.
What happened to him?
I don't know.
He stopped playing?
I don't know. I really don't know. He stopped playing; you don't hear him any more.
He must have stopped a long time ago.
Yes.
The last that's known of him, I think, is with Alphonso Trent.
I don't know. He got sick or something. I don't know. Maybe... I really don't. I have no idea.
Was he a good trombone player, too?
Dickenson - 103
Yes, he was.
He was older than Teddy.
I just don't know. Teddy seemed to tell him what to do all the time. So I really don't know which was the oldest.
I think maybe it's in the back of my mind somewhere that something happened to him mentally, I think.
Well, it could have. It just could have.
But the Speed Webb Band, I guess, with guys like Roy and Teddy and yourself...
Reunald Jones. Do you know Reunald Jones?
Yes.
He was in it.
Was there a trumpet player named Speed Dunn?
Yeah. He's still living. He's in Cincinnati.
